newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Belfox plans medium-term govt bond futures.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Belfox plans medium-term govt bond futures.

text.p: Belgium's futures and options exchange Belfox is aiming to launch derivatives on medium-term Belgian government bonds (OLOs) before the second half of 1997, Belfox management committee president Jos Schmitt said on Monday.
The future would be on three- to five-year bonds comparable to Bobls in Germany, Schmitt told Reuters after a news conference on Belfox's 1996 results.
Demand for such a product had come from the Belgian banking sector, he added.
Earlier the exchange said net income had soared by 80 percent to 93 million Belgian francs in 1996, partly a result of a 16 percent fall in costs.
Overall volume rose 22 percent to 2.6 million lots.

Among equity products Bel-20 stock index .BFX futures volume soared by 74 percent, Bel-20 index options - the most heavily traded product - rose by 36 percent and volume in individual stock options jumped by 66 percent.
But fixed income and currency products turnover fell across the board, with OLO futures turnover down by 23 percent.

Fixed income and currency instruments represented just 36 percent of net income in 1996, a fall from 56 percent on the previous year, while the share contributed by equity products rose to 49 percent from 33 percent in 1995.

Belfox - one of Europe's smaller futures and options exchanges - has said that over the next five years it will focus increasingly on equity-based derivatives because it expects the advent of a single European currency will concentrate trading in fixed income products on bigger financial markets.
"But in 1997, we want to improve turnover and liquidity in all our contracts," Schmitt said.
"At least for two years they (fixed income products) can represent an important service for the financial community and a source of income for Belfox for reinvestment," he added.
Belfox's other objectives for 1997 include a plan to develop indices based on sectors of pan-European stocks, on which it will later launch derivatives.

It is also considering providing clearing services for over the counter (OTC) business, wants to develop more synergies in some areas with the Brussels stock exchange, and plans to have a new trading system operational by the end of the year.
